payload.prfaq: PRESS RELEASE (working backwards): 'Quackitect v2 ships the SE machine: iterations that drive themselves. The owner draws the process as a canvas in Obsidian; the engine compiles the drawing and enforces it at the tool boundary. Agents receive work packets, parallel branches carry two agents at once, and every gate waits for one human bless - on the board today, on the phone next. The laws that used to live in prompts - answer within a second, verify at milestones only, commit only after a bless - are now refusals the machine makes for you.' HOSTILE FAQ: Q1 Over-engineering for one person? A: measured, not felt - four prose-law violations in one morning with a cooperative agent; unattended runs need refusals, not vigilance. Q2 What when the machine is WRONG - a state should be skipped or an offer is stale? A: today, nothing - no dismiss/supersede lane, no skip semantics; WEAK ANSWER, folded into the register (R1, I2). Q3 Why a niche canvas format, not YAML? A: the owner lives in Obsidian; the drawing is the native medium; the compiler pins the format version and refuses loudly. Q4 Executor rewrite breaks the flying iteration? A: R4 - instance git-tracked, restore and resume. Q5 Two agents, one repo - merge hell? A: honestly open - R6, lane rule ruled before enabling. Q6 Why not CI/workflow engines? A: no human-gate-as-state, no owner-drawable source. Q7 Twenty steps, one day? A: R3, split trigger armed on the M6 build plan.
payload.findings_folded: Q2 exposed the weakest answer: the machine has no legal way to be wrong (no skip, no dismiss, no supersede). Folded: R1 sharpened to cover ALL refusal kinds, I2 confirmed as an i3 step, and the M0/M1 sufficiency question this surfaced went straight to the owner (product-level states should be inheritable, not re-filled every iteration - ruling pending). Everything else was already upstream in the register or the plan.
